lists.AI Context Optimization: Repos focused on optimizing what enters an LLM's context window: compression, summarization, pruning, chunk selection, prompt caching, token budgeting, and long-context strategies. Excludes persistent agent memory, RAG/GraphRAG retrieval pipelines, model routing, tool-call orchestration, and inference engines, which belong in sibling Lists.
lists.AI Design Tools: Repositories for AI-powered design creation and assistance: generative graphics, UI/UX mockups, image/logo/brand assets, design-to-code, and AI copilots for designers. Excludes general-purpose UI design tools, UI frameworks, and non-AI design utilities already covered by sibling UI lists.
lists.Agent Harness: Frameworks and runtimes that scaffold, execute, and orchestrate AI agents, including planning loops, tool dispatch, and state management. Excludes agent memory systems, reusable skills, and standalone tool-call implementations.
lists.Agent Memory: Covers systems and libraries that give autonomous agents persistent, episodic, semantic, or working memory, including storage, recall, summarization, and cross-session state. Excludes general RAG/GraphRAG pipelines, context-window optimization, model routing, agent skills, tool-call frameworks, and harnesses unless memory is their primary focus.
lists.Agent Skills: Repositories focused on reusable capabilities that AI agents can invoke, including skill libraries, skill definitions, packaging, discovery, composition, and skill-specific execution patterns. Excludes agent memory, tool-call plumbing, model routing, context optimization, and general agent harnesses or frameworks unless the core contribution is a reusable skill itself.
lists.Agent Tool-call: Repositories for function/tool calling in AI agents: schemas, invocation runtimes, parsers, validators, routers, and evaluation for LLM-generated calls. Excludes agent memory, skills, harnesses, model routing, context optimization, and general backend, database, UI, or automation projects.
lists.Automation (AI Powered): Repositories for automating tasks, workflows, or operations where AI/LLMs are central to the approach. Excludes conventional non-AI-first automation platforms, generic agent frameworks, and tooling better classified under agent skills, tool-call handling, or business tools.
lists.Automation (Non-ai first): Classic, deterministic automation tooling: schedulers, workflow engines, CI/CD, scripting, RPA, cron, and infrastructure orchestration that do not rely on AI/LLM capabilities. Excludes AI-powered automation agents, LLM-driven workflow tools, and agent frameworks, which belong in Automation (AI Powered).
lists.Awesome Lists: Curated “awesome” repositories that collect links to resources on a topic. This List is for meta-lists only; it excludes individual tools, libraries, frameworks, models, or topic-specific projects unless they are themselves curated awesome lists.
lists.Backend Scaling: Repositories and tools for scaling backend services: load balancing, caching, queues, sharding, horizontal scaling, performance tuning, and distributed system infrastructure. Excludes database-specific tools, UI frameworks, LLM routing, inference engines, and agent frameworks.
lists.Business Tools (AI): AI-powered business applications and platforms for operations, sales, marketing, finance, HR, customer support, and analytics. Excludes non-AI business tools, AI design tools, generic automation, agent frameworks, and infrastructure/libraries not directly serving business workflows.
lists.Business Tools (Non-AI): General-purpose business software for operations, finance, CRM, HR, project management, and productivity that does not rely on AI features. Exclude AI-powered business tools, AI automation, developer frameworks, databases, UI libraries, and agent infrastructure.
lists.Database tools: Covers general-purpose database engines, administration clients, migrations, schema tooling, and monitoring across relational and NoSQL systems. Excludes SQLite-specific projects, RAG/GraphRAG pipelines, agent memory stores, and UI or backend-scaling frameworks unless they are primarily database tooling.
lists.Frameworks/libraries: Software development frameworks and libraries that provide reusable code for building applications, including general-purpose, language-specific, and domain libraries. Excludes UI frameworks, programming languages, backend scaling tools, databases, AI agent harnesses, model routing, inference engines, WordPress, local LLM tools, and curated awesome lists.
lists.Inference Engines: Inference Engines covers software that executes or serves LLM and other model inference, including optimized runtimes, serving backends, and local/remote execution libraries. It excludes the models themselves, model routing/selection, general local LLM desktop tooling, and agent or RAG frameworks.
lists.LLM Model Routing: Repositories for dynamically selecting, switching, or cascading among multiple language models based on cost, latency, quality, or task. Not model catalogs, inference servers, context compression, or agent tool-calling.
lists.LLM Models: Repositories containing pretrained or foundation model weights, architectures, training recipes, fine-tuning code, and model cards for large language models. Excludes routing, serving or inference engines, local runners, agent frameworks, and context optimization.
lists.Local LLM tools: Tools for running, serving, fine-tuning, quantizing, and managing LLMs locally on personal or on-prem hardware, including desktop apps, CLIs, and orchestration utilities. Excludes model weights, API routers, RAG pipelines, and standalone inference engines covered by sibling Lists.
lists.Programming Languages: Repositories about language specifications, compilers, interpreters, runtimes, core standard libraries, and language-specific tooling. Excludes general-purpose frameworks, standalone libraries, and type-level utilities, which belong in Frameworks/libraries or Typesafe-Jev.
lists.RAG/GraphRAG: Retrieval-augmented generation systems, vector and graph retrieval pipelines, GraphRAG frameworks, and indexing/query tools for grounding LLM outputs. Excludes general agent memory, context optimization, model routing, inference engines, and standalone databases unless RAG-specific.
lists.SQLite: Repositories centered on SQLite: the engine, extensions, bindings, drivers, WASM builds, and SQLite-specific tools or utilities. Not general database tools, ORMs, or backend scaling projects unless SQLite is the primary subject.
lists.Typesafe-Jev: Repositories about type-safe programming and typed tooling, including type checkers, typed APIs, and compile-time safety. Excludes general programming languages, UI frameworks, database tools, and AI/agent tooling covered by sibling Lists.
lists.UI Design Tools: Tools for UI/UX design: prototyping, wireframing, visual interface editing, design systems, and design handoff. Excludes UI Frameworks and AI Design Tools; this is not for frontend code libraries or AI-specific design generation.
lists.UI Frameworks: Libraries and frameworks for building user interfaces, including component systems, rendering, and frontend app architectures for web, mobile, or desktop. Excludes visual design or prototyping tools, AI design generators, and non-UI general-purpose libraries or languages.
lists.Wordpress: Repositories centered on the WordPress platform: core, plugins, themes, block editor, hosting, and platform-specific tooling or integrations. Excludes general web frameworks, other CMS platforms, and AI/agent tooling unless built specifically for WordPress.
